questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the fiscal framework in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Public capital expenditure of Rs 12.2 lakh crore and a fiscal deficit of 4.3 per cent of GDP were proposed for FY2026-27.
2. The Budget moved away from annual deficit targets towards a debt-to-GDP target of 50 per cent (plus or minus 1) by 2030-31.
3. The revised estimate of the fiscal deficit for FY2025-26 was 4.8 per cent of GDP.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget set capex at Rs 12.2 lakh crore with a 4.3 per cent deficit and anchored policy to a debt-to-GDP target of 50 per cent, give or take 1 point, by 2030-31. The FY2025-26 revised estimate of the deficit was 4.4 per cent, not 4.8 per cent.
questions.h: Deficit 4.3, capex 12.2 lakh crore, debt anchor 50 by 2030-31.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tax changes in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The Income Tax Act, 2025 takes effect from 1 April 2026.
2. Tax Collected at Source under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme was cut to 2 per cent for education, medical purposes and overseas tour packages.
3. The customs duty on dutiable goods imported for personal use was cut from 20 per cent to 10 per cent.
4. The Budget removed all customs duty on 17 cancer medicines and also on all other life-saving drugs.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The first three statements match the Budget: the new Income Tax Act applies from 1 April 2026, LRS-linked TCS fell to 2 per cent for the listed uses, and the personal import duty halved to 10 per cent. Only 17 cancer medicines were exempted, not all life-saving drugs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Orange Economy announcements in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. The Indian Institute of Creative Technologies, Mumbai, will support AVGC content creator labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges.
2. A new National Institute of Design will be set up in the eastern region, in addition to the seven existing NIDs.
3. The term 'Orange Economy' was coined by an Indian economist in the early 2000s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget backed AVGC labs in 15,000 schools and 500 colleges through IICT Mumbai and proposed a new NID in the east, where India has seven NIDs now. The term 'Orange Economy' was popularised by Colombia's former President Ivan Duque and Felipe Buitrago in their 2013 book.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about announcements in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. City Economic Regions will receive Rs 5,000 crore each over five years.
2. A Rs 10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Scheme was announced.
3. Rare Earth Corridors were proposed in Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: City Economic Regions get Rs 5,000 crore each over five years and a Rs 10,000 crore Container Manufacturing Scheme was announced. The rare earth corridors are planned for Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, not Rajasthan and Gujarat.
questions.h: Corridors: Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about infrastructure announcements in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. Seven high-speed rail corridors were announced as growth connectors, including Mumbai-Pune and Hyderabad-Bengaluru.
2. A new Dedicated Freight Corridor from Dankuni to Surat was announced.
3. The share of inland and coastal shipping in the freight mix is to rise from 12 per cent to 6 per cent by 2047.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Seven high-speed rail corridors and a new Dankuni-Surat Dedicated Freight Corridor were announced. The shipping share target runs the other way: from 6 per cent to 12 per cent by 2047. The Budget also announced 20 new national waterways over five years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about support for MSMEs in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. A Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund was created for high-potential enterprises.
2. A Rs 2,000 crore top-up was announced for the Self-Reliant India Fund for micro-enterprises.
3. The Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) was made mandatory for all private-sector purchases from MSMEs.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SME Growth Fund of Rs 10,000 crore and the Rs 2,000 crore Self-Reliant India Fund top-up are both correct. The TReDS mandate applies to purchases by central public sector enterprises from MSMEs, not to all private buyers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the February 2026 meeting of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):
1. The repo rate was kept unchanged at 5.25 per cent.
2. The policy stance was changed to accommodative.
3. The MPC's inflation mandate is 4 per cent with a tolerance band of 2 to 6 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MPC under Governor Sanjay Malhotra held the repo rate at 5.25 per cent with a neutral stance after the 25 basis point cut in December 2025. It also raised its FY26 growth projection to 7.4 per cent. The 4 per cent target with a 2 to 6 per cent band is the legal mandate, so statement 2 alone is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's amended Lending to MSME Sector Directions (February 2026):
1. The collateral-free loan limit for Micro and Small Enterprises was raised from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 20 lakh.
2. It applies to loans sanctioned or renewed on or after 1 April 2026.
3. Units financed under the PMEGP are excluded from the higher limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The limit for collateral-free loans to micro and small enterprises doubled to Rs 20 lakh for loans sanctioned or renewed from 1 April 2026. The limit also applies to units financed under PMEGP, which is implemented by KVIC, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Union Budget 2026-27 proposed a market-making framework, total return swaps on corporate bonds and bond-index derivatives to deepen the corporate bond market.
Statement-II: India's corporate bond market is about 15-16 per cent of GDP, compared with over 80 per cent in the United States, and banks hold roughly 60-65 per cent of non-financial corporate debt.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct, and the second explains the first: a shallow bond market that leaves banks as the main lenders is the reason the Budget sought instruments such as market making and derivatives. The RBI followed with draft rules enabling total return swaps and credit default swaps on corporate bonds.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the new GDP series released by MoSPI on 27 February 2026:
1. The base year was shifted to 2022-23 from 2011-12.
2. Real GDP growth for FY2025-26 was estimated at 7.6 per cent in the Second Advance Estimates.
3. The Q3 growth rate of 7.8 per cent refers to the January-March 2026 quarter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The new series uses 2022-23 as base year and estimates FY2025-26 real growth at 7.6 per cent. Q3 of a financial year is October-December, so the 7.8 per cent rate refers to October-December 2025. Provisional estimates were scheduled for 29 May 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Consumer Price Index released on a new base year in February 2026:
1. The new base year is 2024, replacing 2012.
2. Provisional all-India CPI inflation for January 2026 was 2.75 per cent.
3. The index is released by the Reserve Bank of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: MoSPI, not the RBI, releases the CPI. The new series on base 2024 was released on 12 February 2026 and showed provisional inflation of 2.75 per cent for January 2026. The RBI only uses CPI inflation as its policy target.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the new Consumer Price Index series (base 2024):
1. The weight of food and beverages was cut to 36.75 per cent from 45.86 per cent.
2. The basket was widened from 299 to 358 items.
3. Weights are drawn from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24.
4. New items include rural housing, OTT subscriptions and value-added dairy products.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All four statements are correct. The new series shrinks the food and beverages weight, widens the basket from 299 to 358 items, draws weights from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24 and adds items such as rural housing, OTT subscriptions and value-added dairy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revision of India's merchandise trade indices in February 2026:
1. The base year of the export and import unit value indices was revised from FY2012-13 to FY2022-23.
2. The revised series includes gross, net and income terms of trade.
3. The indices are compiled by MoSPI.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The unit value indices were rebased from FY2012-13 to FY2022-23 and now include gross, net and income terms of trade along with bilateral indices for the top 20 partners. They are compiled by the Directorate General of Commercial Intelligence and Statistics (DGCI&S), not by MoSPI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS):
1. Its outlay was raised from Rs 22,919 crore to Rs 40,000 crore in Budget 2026-27.
2. It is implemented by MeitY and was launched in April 2025.
3. Investment commitments by December 2025 fell short of the initial target of Rs 59,350 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ECMS, run by MeitY since April 2025, had its outlay raised to Rs 40,000 crore. Commitments of Rs 1.15 lakh crore by December 2025 exceeded the initial target of Rs 59,350 crore, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Biopharma SHAKTI announced in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. It has an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore over five years.
2. It envisages three new NIPERs and the upgrading of seven existing ones.
3. It creates a dedicated scientific review cadre in the Indian Council of Medical Research for drug approvals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Biopharma SHAKTI has an outlay of Rs 10,000 crore over five years and plans three new NIPERs and upgrading of seven existing ones, plus a network of over 1,000 accredited clinical trial sites. The scientific review cadre is for the CDSCO, not the ICMR.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about rare earth permanent magnets (REPMs) in the Union Budget 2026-27 context:
1. The REPM Manufacturing Scheme of Rs 7,280 crore targets 6,000 MTPA capacity covering the chain from rare-earth oxides to finished magnets.
2. India imported most of its REPMs from China during 2022-25, about 60-80 per cent by value.
3. The Budget proposed three new chemical parks backed by an allocation of Rs 6,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rs 7,280 crore scheme aims at an integrated REPM ecosystem of 6,000 MTPA, and China supplied about 60-80 per cent of India's REPMs by value in 2022-25. The three new chemical parks carry an allocation of Rs 600 crore, not Rs 6,000 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about manufacturing measures in the Union Budget 2026-27:
1. A dedicated scheme will revive 200 legacy industrial clusters.
2. India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 will focus on fabrication, packaging and equipment.
3. A new Construction and Infrastructure Equipment scheme aims to raise imports of high-value equipment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Budget announced a scheme for 200 legacy industrial clusters and India Semiconductor Mission 2.0 on fabrication, packaging and equipment. The Construction and Infrastructure Equipment scheme seeks to strengthen domestic manufacturing of such equipment, not raise imports.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Export Promotion Mission:
1. Its outlay is Rs 25,060 crore for FY2025-26 to FY2030-31.
2. It is implemented through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade.
3. Niryat Disha is its financial pillar and Niryat Protsahan its non-financial pillar.
4. Export factoring support carries a 2.75 per cent interest subvention capped at Rs 50 lakh per MSME a year.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The outlay, the DGFT role and the factoring subvention are correct. The pillars are reversed: Niryat Protsahan is the financial pillar and Niryat Disha the non-financial one. In February 2026 ten of the eleven interventions were operationalised.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about coking coal being declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral in February 2026:
1. The declaration was made under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957, through Section 11C and amendments to the First Schedule.
2. India imported 57.58 million tonnes of coking coal in 2024-25, mostly from Australia.
3. India is the largest crude steel producer in the world.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The declaration was made under the MMDR Act, 1957 through Section 11C, and imports in 2024-25 were 57.58 million tonnes, mostly from Australia. India is the second-largest crude steel producer, not the largest.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the SIGHT programme under the National Green Hydrogen Mission:
1. It is implemented by MNRE through the Solar Energy Corporation of India.
2. Component II supports green hydrogen and derivatives such as green ammonia through 7 to 10 year offtake agreements.
3. Ammonia liquefies at about minus 253 degrees Celsius, the same as hydrogen.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: SIGHT is run by MNRE through SECI, and Component II backs green hydrogen derivatives like green ammonia with 7 to 10 year offtake agreements. Ammonia liquefies at about minus 33 degrees Celsius, while hydrogen liquefies at below minus 253 degrees, which makes ammonia easier to store and ship.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0, launched on 24 February 2026:
1. Its aggregate monetisation potential is Rs 16.72 lakh crore over FY2025-26 to FY2029-30.
2. It includes Rs 5.8 lakh crore of private investment.
3. NMP 1.0 achieved less than half of its Rs 6 lakh crore target.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NMP 2.0, developed by NITI Aayog under the Asset Monetisation Plan 2025-30, has a potential of Rs 16.72 lakh crore, including Rs 5.8 lakh crore of private investment. NMP 1.0 met nearly 90 per cent of its Rs 6 lakh crore target, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0:
1. The Union Cabinet approved a corpus of Rs 10,000 crore.
2. Fund of Funds 1.0 was managed by SIDBI.
3. Startup India is implemented by the Ministry of MSME.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Cabinet approved a Rs 10,000 crore corpus for early-stage, deep-tech and tech-driven manufacturing startups, and SIDBI managed the first Fund of Funds. Startup India is implemented by DPIIT and was launched on 16 January 2016, not by the Ministry of MSME.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), whose tax collection rates the Union Budget 2026-27 changed for education and medical remittances:
1. Resident individuals, including minors, may remit up to USD 2,50,000 per financial year under it.
2. It was introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in 2004.
3. Corporates and HUFs may use it for current account transactions up to the same limit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LRS lets resident individuals, minors included, remit up to USD 2.5 lakh a year, and the RBI launched it in 2004. It is not available to corporates, partnership firms, HUFs or trusts, and gambling, lottery and speculation remain prohibited.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revised Startup Recognition Framework under the Startup India Action Plan:
1. A recognised startup can be up to 10 years old and have a turnover of up to Rs 200 crore in any financial year, doubled from Rs 100 crore.
2. A new deep tech startup sub-category allows an age limit of 20 years and a turnover limit of Rs 300 crore.
3. Multi-State Cooperative Societies remain ineligible for recognition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The turnover cap was doubled to Rs 200 crore with a 10-year age limit, and deep tech firms get 20 years and Rs 300 crore. Multi-State Cooperative Societies and State-registered cooperative societies were newly included, not excluded.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the financial turnaround of power distribution companies (DISCOMs):
1. DISCOMs recorded a profit after tax of about Rs 2,701 crore in 2024-25, against a loss of Rs 67,962 crore in 2013-14.
2. AT&C losses fell from 22.62 per cent to 15.04 per cent.
3. The Late Payment Surcharge Rules, 2022 let DISCOMs clear legacy dues in up to 12 equated monthly instalments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The profit of Rs 2,701 crore in 2024-25 and the fall in AT&C losses to 15.04 per cent are correct. The LPS Rules, 2022 allowed legacy dues to be cleared in up to 48 equated monthly instalments, not 12; legacy dues fell from Rs 1,39,947 crore in June 2022 to Rs 4,927 crore by January 2026.
